summary: Search query parameter type confusion bypasses the intended 200-character bound and can trigger request failures
evidence: Base routes/search.ts accepted q only when typeof rawCriteria === 'string'. Target routes/search.ts:21 assigns req.query.q as any, and line 22 assumes a string. An anonymous structured q value can therefore reach string-only processing.
context: The target removes the base revision's runtime string guard for the public q query parameter. Express query parsing can produce arrays and objects; these values reach criteria.length and criteria.substring. The unchanged raw SQL interpolation exists in both revisions and is excluded from this diff finding.

validation.method: Static immutable-revision source/control/sink trace; application execution and tests were prohibited by the user.
validation.confidence_rationale: The exact diff, public entrypoint, removed guard, string-only sink, error boundary, and repository fix history form a complete immutable-revision trace with no material reachability gap.
rubric: Anonymous HTTP input reaches the changed value
Base guard is effective and removed in target
Structured query values reach string-only processing
Error propagation and impact boundary are identified
Unchanged intentional SQL injection is excluded
evidence: Target registers an unauthenticated GET route at server.ts:602.
Base accepts q only when typeof rawCriteria is string; target assigns req.query.q directly as any.
Target line 22 assumes .length and .substring on the attacker-selected value.
Repository history commit 068a6b339 identifies the removed guard as the fix for CodeQL alert 32 type confusion.
validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: utils.asyncHandler forwards the synchronous exception to error middleware, limiting demonstrated impact to request-level failure. Application execution was prohibited, so process-wide failure or material cross-user resource exhaustion is unproven.
validation.remaining_uncertainty: No dynamic reproduction was permitted; repeated request-level failures and bounds bypass are established statically, but multi-user service availability impact is not.
validation.source: Anonymous GET /rest/products/search query parameter q at server.ts:602
validation.control: Base typeof rawCriteria === 'string' guard removed at target routes/search.ts:21
validation.sink: criteria.length and criteria.substring at routes/search.ts:22 before SQL query construction
preconditions: Attacker can make an anonymous request to /rest/products/search
q is supplied as a structured query value such as an object or duplicate-key array

attack_path.dataflow: HTTP query string q -> Express req.query.q -> criteria assigned as any at routes/search.ts:21 -> criteria.length / criteria.substring at line 22 -> request exception or character-bound bypass -> SQL construction at line 23.
attack_path.reachability: Anonymous remote attacker can send a structured q query value to the public GET /rest/products/search route; the value reaches target routes/search.ts:21-22 without runtime string narrowing.
attack_path.counterevidence: utils.asyncHandler at lib/utils.ts:229-230 forwards synchronous exceptions to error middleware installed at server.ts:681-682. This strongly confines demonstrated impact to request processing; no process-wide crash, cross-user data impact, or material shared-service exhaustion is established.
attack_path.severity_rationale: The path is public and low-friction, but the proven impact is a deterministic request-level failure and bypass of the intended 200-character bound. With low impact and high likelihood, the required matrix yields low severity (P3).
attack_path.change_conditions: The base revision accepted q only when typeof rawCriteria === 'string'. The target removes that guard. Exploitation requires only normal public route exposure and Express query parsing of a structured value.
attack_path.cross_boundary_behavior: Remote input crosses the HTTP trust boundary into the runtime handler; no victim, privilege, or data boundary beyond the initiating request is demonstrated.
attack_path.preconditions: Attacker can reach the public route and encode q as an object or duplicate-key array.
attack_path.impact_surface: runtime availability and input-bound enforcement in one service
attack_path.blindspots: Dynamic reproduction was prohibited; broader availability degradation under volume remains unproven.
attack_path.controls: Promise wrapper and centralized error middleware contain the synchronous exception.
